objective: Proof: the double of that handlebody is a closed orientable 3-manifold with an explicit presentation; with every edge repeated k times its number of homomorphisms into a fixed finite group is an exponential polynomial in k, and for S3 the coefficient of 9^(mk) equals 2 P(G,9)/3^|V| (proper 9-colourings, as pairs of 3-colourings), by a Potts duality on the dual graph; the same holds for every dihedral group (the order-16 one included), for the quaternion group and for A4 with other colour numbers; hence counting homomorphisms from closed 3-manifold groups into these groups is #P-hard, and the bounded-H2 hypothesis in the class-2 nilpotent algorithm of Samperton and Weiss cannot be dropped; standard-library checks against independently identified manifolds, exact coefficient identities and end-to-end interpolation.
status: Proved by HARD-3D-20261025-001B-P001: doubles of fin handlebodies over plane multigraphs are closed orientable 3-manifolds whose counts of homomorphisms into a finite group are exponential polynomials in the edge multiplicity; the target coefficient is a chromatic polynomial (2 P(G,9)/3^|V| for S3, pairs of 3-colourings by Potts duality; analogues for dihedral groups, Q8, A4), so counting homomorphisms from closed 3-manifold groups into S3, every dihedral group whose order is not a power of 2 at least 16, Q8 and A4 is #P-hard (Turing); the class-2 cases show the bounded-H2 hypothesis of Samperton and Weiss is necessary; the order-16 dihedral group is left open (base collision, contamination 192 on the 4-cycle).
title: Closed manifolds: the doubles count pairs of colourings
